As a consistency check, the asset hashes in the packet (RoomCameraHero 6f6c35cc..., StudyRecordSupport 5aefbe45...) match the story_art.entries, native_media and film_direction.renderer_inputs rows inside both treatment boards. The packet's board sha256 equals opening-a's, so I treated storyboard.json as byte-identical to opening-a.json and did not read it separately.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: Intended chain, from code (not observed): in a generic illustrated Houston cardiothoracic operating room, four wall cameras light and watch a gurney roll in. A wall clock ring is stamped by pulses from a camera at entry, draping and turnover. A draped patient triggers an amber 'Patient draped' text on a surgeon's phone. A study card shows the suite line pulling away from other Houston Methodist sites while 25 case tiles pour into a tray. A 7 percent badge and a 8.3 to 41.0 interval whisker follow, then a placebo row with a 'short of conventional significance' stamp and an 'associated, not caused' card with a struck 'caused' arrow. Bundled review notes and a minority stake ring come next, then a future-work card tagging turnover, and finally a blank turnover box as the camera lamps dim.
story_review.opening_to_ending: It opens on 'Does a camera that logs an operating room add surgeries, or only count them?' over a room that only brightens. The answer actually arrives at s7 (about 25 more, associated rather than caused). The film then closes on a blank turnover box and dimming camera lamps. As built, the close asks whether turnover sped up rather than visibly tying that open question back to the 25 added cases, and the dimming lamps add an unsupported implication that the cameras were switched off.
story_review.weakest_transition: s2 to s3 (12.48 s). The draped patient is rolled out and the table reset with a fresh sheet. Then, with no arrival, an identical undraped patient lies on a sheetless table and is draped again under 'It also texted the surgeon when the patient was draped'. The declared bridge (the Draped marker lifts off the ring as the phone lights) is not implemented.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: Intended chain, from code (not observed): a floor plan of a generic Houston operating room brightens under a suite plate. A cut to wall height shows four cameras lighting, and on the plan a gurney enters under their sight wedges. A ruled 'Room clock record' ledger stamps entry, draping and turnover row by row, then an overhead plan stamps turnover as the patient leaves. A desk phone in a gloved hand lights and receives 'Patient draped' after a split-screen draping. The same study, percent, interval, placebo, associated-not-caused, bundle and stake boards follow on a ledger page. A future-work card tags turnover, and the film ends on a blank turnover box on the ledger in front of the room as its camera lamps dim.
story_review.opening_to_ending: It opens on the same question as A, but over a static plan, so the 'number first' promise is never shown. The answer arrives at s7. It closes on a blank turnover box on a desk ledger with the room's lamps dimming behind it. The ledger framing makes the record look hand-kept, which undercuts the 'camera logs the room' premise the ending relies on, and the close does not tie the open turnover question back to the 25 added cases.
story_review.weakest_transition: s2 to s3 (12.48 to 14.66 s). The overhead plan leaves the drape stranded on an empty table as the patient rides out on the gurney. The cut goes to a desk phone with no table, and then a split shows an identical undraped patient back on the table being draped again. Identity, the reset state and cause are all broken across the handoff.

consolidated_correction: Opening (both): make the cameras act within 1.5 s (lamps light, heads track the arriving gurney) while the plate settles. For B, either implement the declared counter-first opening or correct its angle, opening_promise, divergence_note and registry note.
Entry stamp (both): stamp 'Patient entry' as the gurney crosses into the room, on the clock, in one shot. Do not label the table transfer as entry.

Drape, gurney and transfers (both, shared RoomCameraHero): give the drape continuous identity and support (it exists before it moves, placed by visible anonymous gloved hands or another supported path), and give the gurney push and patient transfers the same agent.
Hand (both, shared GlovedHand): join the thumb root to a visible palm or wrist, and verify at scales .8, .95, 1.45, 1.5 and 1.55.

s2 to s3 continuity (both, clockState): either stay on the same draped case at the draping moment, or visibly bring in the next patient. Do not erase the reset sheet or teleport a patient onto the table.
Event-in-shot timing (both): move the frozen scene_fraction cut points so s2-event-3, s6-event-2 and s9-event-2 each complete within one shot, especially the Draped stamp.
Placebo row (both, StudyRecordSupport S6B): 10 placebo bars plus the suite bar, and either a verified rank claim or rank-neutral heights.

Ending (both): keep the camera lamps lit (use room light if any dimming is wanted) and bring the s4/s7 result (about 25 more, the associated link) into the closing composition beside the blank turnover box.
A only: remove the shot-1 to shot-2 camera re-posing in s1 (one consistent set of mounts, plus a real viewpoint change if a cut is kept).

B only: show a camera causing each s2 stamp and do not stage the record as a hand-kept ledger. Make the overhead turnover drape travel with the patient and show the reset. Reframe ledger-company-close and ledger-stake-detail so the camera company tag is in the picture box while the slice lights.

Prose only (both, non-blocking): correct the story_contract visible_bridge sentences, shot carry text, camera_strategy fields and 'continuous' transition labels so they match the renderer, or implement them.
